title: Sam Altman: Care about opinions on a long time horizon, because being misunderstood is a strength
summary: Altman reframes "how do I stop caring what people think" as the wrong question. You choose whose opinions matter and on what timescale. The most impressive people care on a very long horizon, accept short-term low status, and use being misunderstood as room to solve important problems.

principles.text: Don't try to stop caring what others think; choose whose opinions matter and on what subjects.
principles.quote: Almost everyone cares what someone thinks (though caring what everyone thinks is definitely a mistake), and it's probably important. Caring too much makes you a sheep.

principles.text: You still need to be somewhat in tune with others to build something useful for them.
principles.quote: But you need to be at least a little in tune with others to do something useful for them.

principles.text: Timescale is a second lever: most people pick whose opinions count but ignore the time horizon.
principles.quote: you can choose the people whose opinions you care about (and on what subjects), and you can choose the timescale you care about them on.

principles.text: Care about opinion on a very long horizon; let the newspapers get it wrong if history gets it right.
principles.quote: they generally care about other people’s opinions on a very long time horizon—as long as the history books get it right, they take some pride in letting the newspapers get it wrong.

principles.text: Trade short-term low status for long-term high status, usually via an eventually-right non-consensus bet.
principles.quote: You should trade being short-term low-status for being long-term high-status, which most people seem unwilling to do.

principles.text: If you're right, being misunderstood gives you and a few rebels space to solve important problems.
principles.quote: as long as you are right, being misunderstood by most people is a strength not a weakness. You and a small group of rebels get the space to solve an important problem that might otherwise not get solved.
